defect: 5 bars at strokeWeight=1.2 with tight spacing; at 16px the bars still have a distinct silhouette but individual bar separation is harder to read than 3- or 4-bar variants
suggested_fix: prefer A1 or A3 for small-size contexts

defect: 6 bars at strokeWeight=1.0 with spacing=0.15; at 16px the 6 fine bars risk merging into a grey block; individual bar count is not readable at favicon scale
suggested_fix: best used at 32px and above; consider A3 or A1 for favicons

defect: six fine bars at 16px in avatar crop produce a near-indistinct rectangular mass — density works against distinctiveness at this scale

3 steps with wide rounded corners reads as a generic progress-bar or loading indicator — the rounding softens the architectural staircase character that makes Direction B distinctive; risks generic tech UI association
suggested_fix: sharper corners (curvature 0 or 0.02) would restore the staircase reading

defect: 6 steps at stepWidth=0.18 produce very fine columns (~7px each at 16px); the individual steps merge into a boxy shape at favicon scale; not clearly a staircase from the mark alone
suggested_fix: use at 32px+ only; B1 or B2 are stronger favicon choices

defect: at 96px avatar crop, 6 fine columns produce a rectangular block rather than a readable staircase silhouette — density hurts distinctiveness

at 16px the 3 staggered arcs with 30° offset produce a filled silhouette with a notch cutout — readable as a shape but the arcs individual character is lost; reads as a simplified bird/flag rather than layered arcs
suggested_fix: increase stroke width or reduce arc count for clearer arc reading at small sizes

defect: the notch creates an irregular silhouette that is distinctive but may read as a specific object (bird, direction arrow) rather than an abstract brand mark; distinctive is good but may be too specific

the 3-arc staggered shape with notch at 30° offset produces an organic-looking silhouette that edges toward naturalistic imagery; less like 'data layers' and more like a fauna silhouette — inconsistent with the Prisma/Vercel family aesthetic
suggested_fix: reduce offset or use symmetric arcs to maintain abstract quality

defect: 2 concentric arcs at 270° sweep with no rotational offset reads exactly as a progress ring or loading spinner — one of the most common UI metaphors in dev tooling; risks instant 'loading state' association rather than brand mark
suggested_fix: add a rotational offset, reduce sweep to 200°, or use 3+ arcs to differentiate from loading-spinner tropes

defect: 4 arcs at 150° sweep with 45° offsets produce a complex multi-notch silhouette; at 16px the arcs merge into an irregular filled shape with multiple jagged cutouts — legible as something but the arc motif is lost
suggested_fix: reduce arcCount to 2-3 or increase stroke width for better small-scale reading

defect: 4 short arcs with 45° offsets produce a complex notched-bird silhouette at 96px; while immediately distinctive, it reads as an object/creature rather than an abstract data motif

the 4-arc 45°-offset shape strongly resembles a bird or directional arrow — the organic-irregular silhouette conflicts with the precise Geist typographic aesthetic; 'well-made dev tooling' expects geometric abstraction not organic forms
suggested_fix: the motif concept (layered arcs) is correct for brand DNA but the specific rendering at 4×45° offset reads too naturalistic

defect: Direction D typemarks have no separate mark element — at 16px the full 'accrue' wordmark is near-illegible (letterforms are 3-4px tall); the cc-echo effect at dx=4 is imperceptible at favicon scale; Direction D is lockup-only, not a favicon candidate
suggested_fix: Direction D is appropriate for README header and social card contexts; 16px use requires a mark-only favicon variant (not present)

defect: cc-echo at opacity=0.35 produces a grey ghost in monochrome; the ghost echo has low contrast against the paper background and may disappear in some monochrome contexts (print, high-contrast mode)
suggested_fix: increase echo opacity to 0.5+ or use a darker echo fill for monochrome safety

defect: avatar crop of the full 'accrue' typemark at 96px shows large bold letterforms filling the frame — legible but not distinguishable from plain text in a circular crop; the cc-echo motif is too subtle at this scale
suggested_fix: a mark-only avatar variant (just the 'cc' pair) would serve better

defect: the stepped-e crossbar notch (stepDepth=28) is imperceptible at 16px — letterforms are too small; Direction D is lockup-only, not a favicon candidate
suggested_fix: Direction D candidates need a mark-only favicon; 16px dimension is not the appropriate evaluation axis for integrated typemarks

defect: full typemark in avatar crop shows 'accrue' text clearly but the stepped-e crossbar motif is invisible at 96px; reads as plain Geist wordmark with no distinguishing mark element
suggested_fix: a mark-only or 'cc' pair avatar would be needed for avatar use

defect: u-fill interval at fillLevel=0.55 with Fog (#E9EEF2) fill: at 16px the letterforms are too small to read and the fill detail is invisible; Direction D is lockup-only
suggested_fix: same as D1/D2 — Direction D candidates need a mark-only favicon variant

defect: full typemark in avatar crop; the Fog fill in the u bowl is visible at 96px as a subtle light tone — the effect reads as intended at this scale (vessel/accumulation metaphor in the u) but the overall crop is text rather than a mark symbol
all three motifs combined: cc echo + stepped e crossbar + u fill; at 16px all effects are invisible; same lockup-only limitation as D1-D3
suggested_fix: Direction D candidates are lockup-only; favicon use requires a mark-only variant

defect: Fog fill (#E9EEF2) in the u bowl is very close to Paper (#FAFBFC) in monochrome — the fill interval detail effectively disappears in grayscale contexts; the u bowl reads as empty/unfilled
suggested_fix: replace Fog fill with a mid-grey (#AAAAAA or similar) for monochrome-safe u fill interval

defect: full typemark in avatar crop; all three motif effects compound into a high-density mark that paradoxically reduces at small size; the motif density that makes D4 interesting at large size works against it in 96px crop
